cases.rationale: Re4 permits Nf5+ followed by Qf6, with forcing pressure on the exposed king and a repeatable route to winning h6. Nxd4 removes the checking knight.
Bf5 is the best supplied recorded choice.
Rbg8 leaves Black without timely queenside counterplay. The b4 line opens c5 and leaves d6 exposed, while Na4 enables ...b5 and ...c4.
g5 is the best supplied recorded choice.
Nc4 concedes the tempo to centralize with ...Ke6 or redirect the knight via ...Nb5. c6 makes the passer immediate and constrains Black's pieces.
Kf3 is the best supplied recorded choice.
Qxd6 allows ...Bd4+ Rf2 and rook swings to b6/g6 while White's rook remains tied to the checking diagonal. The pawn gain comes at a concrete cost in forcing king pressure.
cxd5 is the best supplied recorded choice.
Both king moves allow the queen exchange. After Kh1 the ...Bf2 attack on e1 continues with ...Bxe1 and ...Bxe4, while the Kh2 continuation can take e5 before the exchange.
Rfe1 is the best supplied recorded choice.
Rhg7 gives White g4 first, blocking the available ...g4 space gain and delaying Black's planned kingside break.
Nc7 is within seven centipawns of the alternative and reaches the same ...b6 setup.
Bxd4 permits Qd5+, a check that also attacks the bishop on d4. ...Rf7 Qxd4 wins the bishop.
Ne1 and Nd2 are close, within 12 centipawns in the paired search.
Rd2 omits the active Rd8+ and Rd7 pressure on f7. ...Kf8/...Ra4 or ...e4 gives Black the active rook and central pawn advance.
Rxd1 is the best supplied recorded choice.
Bb7 permits Nxd6 and a queen trade on f3 in which White retains the extra minor piece. The active Rxf7 alternative recovers the knight and leads to a materially different sequence.
exd6 is the best supplied recorded choice.
Rxb6 allows the Qa1+–Qe5+–Qe1+ series. Rf2 and Rxg2+ then take the queen for a rook rather than permitting a safe return to the original arrangement.
Qd2 is the best supplied recorded choice.
Rc2+ gives White Kd5 and an active king supporting the c-pawn. The ...hxg4 alternative lets Black reach e6 before that king takes over; the precise tactical share of the pawn race is unclear.
Kxg7 is the best supplied recorded choice.
fxg7 allows ...Kxg7. Be4 first preserves the f6 passer and h7 pressure. The ...h6 line confirms the fxg7 and gxf8 promotion sequence.
f5 and h3 have the same paired score.
Ra8 leaves the e7 bishop pinned to the king and allows Bc5 followed by Bxe7+ and Rxa6. Ke6 breaks the pin and supplies the separate ...Rd8 ...Bc5+ counterplay.
Nc2 is the best supplied recorded choice.
Both Nxe8 and Ba3 win an exchange initially. The engine gap survives the paired search, but distinct later king-safety and pawn trades make a single cause uncertain.
Be6 is the best supplied recorded choice.
Na3 permits ...Nf3+ and the queen's cleared path from c4 to e4. The independent reply maintains the forcing advantage and pawn gains.
c5 is the best supplied recorded choice.
dxc4 allows Rxe4. Both searches retain the knight-for-pawn loss after the e-file trade and see lasting pressure; the alternative starts with ...Na5 and avoids that immediate capture.
Qd6 is the best supplied recorded choice.
Qxd7 permits ...Bg3 while f2 is pinned to the e2 king by the queen on g2. ...Rxe3 and ...Qxf2+ maintain the forcing attack after the exchanges.
Qe5 is the best supplied recorded choice.

limitations: Reviewed from the legal paired principal variations and independently searched replies before opening classifier or model output.
One engine-assisted reviewer with a finite search horizon. Unclear causes remain unknown.
The broadcast cp swing was used for sampling only. The review is tied to the actual move and separates tactical or positional evidence.
The source split groups whole events. Each included game contributes a selected substantial broadcast loss and one near-best control.
